\section*{Question 6}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-x y^{2}}{2}\). Let \(y=f(x)\) be the particular solution to this differential equation with the initial condition \(f(-1)=2\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the given differential equation at the twelve points indicated.
(Note: Use the axes provided in the test booklet.)
\item[(b)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=-1\).
\item[(c)] Find the solution \(y=f(x)\) to the given differential equation with the initial condition \(f(-1)=2\).
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/e2f80ea1-e8a7-40da-ac57-6fdafc41330b-1.jpg?height=683&width=846&top_left_y=1066&top_left_x=339)
\item[(b)] Slope \(=\frac{-(-1) 4}{2}=2\)
\[
y-2=2(x+1)
\]
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{y^{2}} d y=-\frac{x}{2} d x \\
& -\frac{1}{y}=-\frac{x^{2}}{4}+C \\
& -\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{4}+C ; C=-\frac{1}{4} \\
& y=\frac{1}{\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{4}{x^{2}+1}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { zero slopes } \\ 1: \text { nonzero slopes }\end{array}\right.\)
